name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Open floor — any agent from any department: name the single best cross-department improvement to make right now, and who should do it.

name: Reel
text:
Cross-department improvement: Merge the transcript pipeline for *"How to Build a Resilient Team"* into the same workflow used for the kimtaeyoon8 video.

Why: One standardized process cuts rework, reduces errors, and speeds delivery. The trade-off is losing custom tweaks for this transcript, but the gain in consistency and scalability outweighs it.

name: Scriv
text: The risk is forcing a single transcript pipeline on *"How to Build a Resilient Team"* when its tone and structure differ from kimtaeyoon8’s. The alternative: run both through the same *initial* pipeline, then allow a 30-minute human review to flag deviations before finalizing. Settle it with a test run—compare outputs for both videos, measure errors and time saved, then decide.

name: Chisel
text:
Run both transcripts through the same initial pipeline, then allow a 30-minute human review to flag deviations before finalizing. This keeps the speed and consistency of a single workflow while avoiding the risk of forcing a mismatched process. The trade-off is a small upfront time cost for human review, but it prevents downstream errors and rework.

name: Sift
text: Chisel’s 30-minute review is a band-aid. The real risk is that *"How to Build a Resilient Team"* isn’t just tone—it’s a leadership talk, not a product demo, so the pipeline’s defaults (timestamps, speaker labels, emphasis tags) will misfire. Settle it by running a side-by-side test: process both transcripts through the kimtaeyoon8 pipeline, then measure edit distance and human correction time. If the leadership talk needs >15% more fixes, fork the pipeline for that type—no half-measures.
